title: Mamba-Sea: A Mamba-Based Framework With Global-to-Local Sequence Augmentation for Generalizable Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Domain generalisation via global appearance augmentation plus sequence-wise local style perturbation: resample feature mean/std inside random contiguous token sub-sequences to suppress domain-specific cues.
adaptation: Treat the 5 sources as training domains and E1 as the unseen domain. The local style perturbation is architecture-agnostic: apply it to ResNet-34 stage-1/2 feature maps over random row or column strips (half-cut scuffs are streaks), on the house PF model, at training time only.
min_experiment: House PF + strip-wise feature style resampling, 3 seeds v house PF 3 seeds. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU, test crack IoU must not drop >0.012. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 and E1 inactive IoU < +0.03.
evidence: R: first method above 90% Dice on the multi-site Prostate DG benchmark (prior SOTA 88.61%).
prior_overlap: Per-panel BN adaptation and intensity normalisation failed, but those are test-time; training-time style perturbation never tested. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Treat the 5 sources as training domains and E1 as the unseen target. Add the sequence-wise token-style perturbation to the bottleneck of Swin-UMamba or RWKV-UNet. Skip any global intensity augmentation that blurs 1 px lines.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Swin-UMamba (or RWKV-UNet) with and without sequence-wise style augmentation, 3 seeds, plus leave-one-source-out folds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU. Kill: under +0.02 E1 relF1@2.
